additives.notes: Highly processed glucose polymer used as filler, binder, and carrier in supplements. GI 85-105 makes it metabolically equivalent to glucose. In vitro data suggests potential gut barrier effects but clinical significance at supplement doses is uncertain. Low severity: the high glycemic impact is a nutritional concern (like added sugar) rather than a toxicological hazard, matching other caloric filler ingredients.
additives.mechanism_of_harm: Highly processed glucose polymer (DE 3-20) with glycemic index 85-105, comparable to pure glucose. Rapidly digested to glucose in the small intestine. additives.notes: Highly processed glucose polymer used as filler, binder, and carrier in supplements. GI 85-105 makes it metabolically equivalent to glucose. In vitro data suggests potential gut barrier effects but clinical significance at supplement doses is uncertain. Low severity: the high glycemic impact is a nutritional concern (like added sugar) rather than a toxicological hazard, matching other caloric filler ingredients.
additives.mechanism_of_harm: Highly processed glucose polymer (DE 3-20) with glycemic index 85-105, comparable to pure glucose. Rapidly digested to glucose in the small intestine. In vitro studies suggest maltodextrin may suppress antimicrobial defense mechanisms and promote E. coli adhesion to intestinal epithelial cells (PMID 23251695 (Nickerson & Chang 2012 PLoS One)). Used as cheap filler/binder in supplements with no nutritional benefit.

IBD (Crohn's disease) — in vitro evidence of impaired antimicrobial defense and promoted E. coli adhesion (PMID 23251695)

additives.notes: Magnesium stearate is an FDA GRAS flow agent present in the vast majority of supplement tablets and capsules. It prevents powders from sticking to manufacturing equipment. Internet claims that it blocks nutrient absorption are not supported by clinical evidence — the single study cited used unrealistic concentrations. Stearic acid (its main component) is a natural fatty acid found in chocolate, meat, and dairy. Penalized at low severity only as a non-nutritive processing aid, not as a health concern.
additives.mechanism_of_harm: FDA GRAS flow agent (lubricant) used in virtually all tablet and capsule manufacturing. Facilitates powder flow through equipment. Claims of bioavailability reduction are based on a single in-vitro dissolution study (Brittain 2002) at unrealistically high concentrations; multiple subsequent studies found no meaningful effect on absorption at typical 0.5-2% levels. Stearic acid is a common dietary saturated fat found in cocoa butter and meat.
population_warnings: No specific population warnings — safe at typical supplement levels

harmful_additives.notes: Highly processed glucose polymer used as filler, binder, and carrier in supplements. GI 85-105 makes it metabolically equivalent to glucose. In vitro data suggests potential gut barrier effects but clinical significance at supplement doses is uncertain. Low severity: the high glycemic impact is a nutritional concern (like added sugar) rather than a toxicological hazard, matching other caloric filler ingredients.
harmful_additives.mechanism_of_harm: Highly processed glucose polymer (DE 3-20) with glycemic index 85-105, comparable to pure glucose. Rapidly digested to glucose in the small intestine. In vitro studies suggest maltodextrin may suppress antimicrobial defense mechanisms and promote E. coli adhesion to intestinal epithelial cells (PMID 23251695 (Nickerson & Chang 2012 PLoS One)). Used as cheap filler/binder in supplements with no nutritional benefit.
population_warnings: Diabetes or insulin resistance — GI 85-105, causes rapid blood glucose spikes comparable to pure glucose
IBD (Crohn's disease) — in vitro evidence of impaired antimicrobial defense and promoted E. coli adhesion (PMID 23251695)
Celiac disease — wheat-derived maltodextrin may contain trace gluten

harmful_additives.notes: Magnesium stearate is an FDA GRAS flow agent present in the vast majority of supplement tablets and capsules. It prevents powders from sticking to manufacturing equipment. Internet claims that it blocks nutrient absorption are not supported by clinical evidence — the single study cited used unrealistic concentrations. Stearic acid (its main component) is a natural fatty acid found in chocolate, meat, and dairy. Penalized at low severity only as a non-nutritive processing aid, not as a health concern.
harmful_additives.mechanism_of_harm: FDA GRAS flow agent (lubricant) used in virtually all tablet and capsule manufacturing. Facilitates powder flow through equipment. Claims of bioavailability reduction are based on a single in-vitro dissolution study (Brittain 2002) at unrealistically high concentrations; multiple subsequent studies found no meaningful effect on absorption at typical 0.5-2% levels. Stearic acid is a common dietary saturated fat found in cocoa butter and meat.
population_warnings: No specific population warnings — safe at typical supplement levels

harmful_additives.mechanism_of_harm: Amorphous silicon dioxide (SiO2) used as anti-caking agent in tablets/capsules at <2% w/w. FDA GRAS (21 CFR 172.480, max 2% of food weight). EFSA 2018 re-evaluation could not confirm safety due to insufficient nanoparticle characterization data — this was a data gap, not a finding of harm. Amorphous SiO2 is poorly absorbed from the GI tract. Nanoparticle concerns are based on in vitro studies at concentrations far exceeding dietary exposure.
